Licorice pseudoaldosteronism / hypokalaemia case reports. Fatigue is the presenting symptom; direction correct.

Most papers are not about mugwort: citrus red mite, garlic anaphylaxis, cow's milk allergy, canary food mix. Mugwort appears only in standard allergen panels.
Mixed relevance - asparagus allergy and generic herbal-usage surveys counted as garlic/asthma.

Ankaferd Blood Stopper papers legitimately contain licorice. Human n=3 with one wrong-plant match.

Human papers are a school allergy survey, autumn crocus poisoning and a Salmonella outbreak - none about garlic and diarrhoea.
Multi-herb attribution: TCM formulas containing licorice counted as licorice studies.
Flagship pair: 104 preclinical at 99% positive vs 5 decided human at 60%. Most human papers are neutral, which is why human n is small.
Papers do not support the pairing: ginger-for-nausea trial, Alpinia galanga erectile dysfunction, curcumin postpartum depression.
'weight loss' conflates cachexia (harmful) with intentional weight loss (beneficial); one preclinical paper is cancer-induced adipose wasting.
Papers are chamomile for cancer TREATMENT SIDE EFFECTS (mucositis, nausea), not anticancer activity.
Genuine pomegranate seed oil diabetes trials plus Zucker rat work. 'diabetic' is adjectival but unambiguous.
Haemorrhoid/flavonoid-fraction and menopause papers are not about itching.
'weight gain' here is broiler and layer growth performance - a livestock production outcome, not a disease.
Human side solid (turmeric DILI with jaundice). Both preclinical papers are unrelated to jaundice.
Genuine chamomile occupational allergy signal; one multi-herb asthma trial inflates the positive side.
Classic confounder: safflower oil is the n-6 CONTROL DIET in these rodent fatty-acid studies, not the intervention.
Genuine cardamom chemoprevention work (azoxymethane ACF, benzo[a]pyrene forestomach).
'proinflammatory' is a mechanism word, not a disease.
'Allium vegetables are associated with REDUCED risk of colorectal cancer' is labelled negative. The sentiment layer conflates an inverse association with a harmful one.
Preclinical STZ/alloxan rat work is genuine; the single human paper is a chemical burn case report.
Melissa papers are mostly protection against chemo toxicity, not anticancer. A foliar-fertiliser agronomy paper is tiered in-vitro.

Several Sambucus lectin papers use SNA as a laboratory REAGENT rather than studying elderflower.
'fever' is a symptom; the papers are broadly about COVID-19 supplements.
Genuine licorice hepatoprotection in rodents. Entirely preclinical (human n=0) - the contrast with turmeric pairs 1 and 18 is the point.
Genuine peppermint aromatherapy anxiety RCTs and systematic reviews.
'blood stasis' is a TCM diagnostic concept, not a clinical outcome. 100% positive across 31 papers with no negative finding at all.
Fenugreek lipid meta-analyses plus rodent steatosis work. Coherent.
Genuine Nigella sativa glycaemic studies; one COVID supplement paper is off-topic.
'fungal' is an adjective, not a disease, and most papers are crop protection (palmyrah decay fungi, Fusarium, Metarhizium).
Seven tier-1 systematic reviews on cinnamon glycaemic control. The strongest-evidence pair in the sample.
Genuine amla diabetes work; one pomegranate-metabolite paper is misattributed.
'chronic diseases' is an umbrella term, not an outcome. Papers range from ZnO nanoparticles to a diet-and-cancer-risk review.
'platelet aggregation' is a mechanism rather than a disease, though clinically meaningful. Papers are genuinely about Ligusticum antithrombotics.
Consistent licorice compound work on colorectal cancer. Entirely preclinical (human n=0).
Genuine saffron cardiovascular work; two papers (crocin antidepressant, crocetin mast cell) are not cardiovascular.

Genuine Angelica / ligustilide memory studies. Entirely preclinical (human n=0).
Genuine tamarind STZ-rat diabetes work; the two ethnobotanical surveys are neutral and do not affect the ratio.
Mostly genuine curcumin HCC work, but 'Safranal Prevents Liver Cancer' is a saffron paper attributed to turmeric.
